hypothesis: A lateral step in a windowed radial-power-spectrum depth-to-source-ensemble estimate (Spector & Grant 1970 single-slope method) computed only from the cached RTP magnetic band marks a blind basement-offsetting normal fault missing from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue, independent of the amplitude/tilt/Euler-style spatial-domain methods already tested and found negative in this repository.
mechanism: 32x32 px (3.2 km) non-overlapping Hann-tapered blocks of RTP; 2D FFT; 16-bin azimuthally averaged radial power spectrum; linear fit of ln(amplitude) vs wavenumber over bins 1-8; depth = -slope (clipped to [100, 4000] m); nearest-neighbour fill of under-covered blocks; bilinear resample to the full 100 m grid; Gaussian smooth (sigma=4 px); spatial gradient magnitude is the candidate surface. Dots: top-ranked pixels, greedy Poisson-disk placement (min separation 2.8 px), budget 37,654 dots to match the family convention, emitted on the whole footprint minus visible/withheld catalogue pixels per fold.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Volcanic edifices/calderas with a locally shallow source population but no bounding structural offset; GeoDAWN flight-line tie-spacing aliasing at the 3.2 km block's Nyquist scale.
measured_caveat: The fitted depths cluster narrowly (103-394 m, mean 242 m, median 260 m; evidence/h82spec_e1_surface.json) rather than spanning the full clipped range up to 4000 m. A 3.2 km window with the chosen fit band (bins 1-8 of 16) is evidently resolving near-surface magnetic-source texture rather than a genuinely deep, regional Curie-isotherm-scale signal; this instrument is therefore honestly a shallow relative source-depth-texture proxy, not a calibrated regional Curie-point-depth map (that stricter two-depth centroid method is H82S-2, not attempted this session).
